newsitem.title: MEXICO: Opposition ahead in 2 cities in Mexico vote - media.
newsitem.headline: Opposition ahead in 2 cities in Mexico vote - media.

text.p: The Guerrero State Electoral Council said partial results in local elections held Sunday showed two of the state's largest cities falling to the opposition, media reported Monday.

The leftist Democratic Revolution Party (PRD) looked set to win the town hall of Iguala and the pro-business National Action Party, or PAN, was ahead in the city of Taxco, TV network Televisa reported.

Aside these two setbacks for the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), the ruling party was winning in most town hall races, the state news agency Notimex said. although another blow for the PRI was widespread abstension.
Partial counts of around 50 percent of the votes cast also revealed widespread abstensions, of between 50 to 60 percent, according to various Mexico City dailies.
In results released, the PRI led counts in the state capital Chilpancingo, the resort of Acapulco and the towns of Arcelia, Copala, Tlapa, Chilapa and Jose Azueta, Notimex said.
In Chilpancingo, the PRI had 14,997 votes so far, more than double the PRD, and far ahead of the 1,645 votes for by the PAN, Televisa said.
In Acapulco, Guerrero's largest city of more than 1 million people, the PRI had 32,636 votes to date compared to the PRD's 29,012 and the PAN's 11,292 votes, the network added.
In the coastal resort Zihuatanejo, the PRI had a healthy lead of 5,213 votes against the PRD's 646 and the PAN's 828 votes, Televisa said.
In the grubby inland city of Iguala, the state's third largest city, the PRD totaled 12,346 votes so far against the PRI's 9,364 and the PAN's 839, the pro-government television said.

In Taxco, Mexico's inland tourist city famous for its silverware, the conservative PAN party obtained 7,547 votes counted to so far, a slender lead over the PRI's 6,078 votes and the PRD's 1,882 votes, it added.

Fears of violence may have kept many voters at home. PRI officials estimated half of registered voters stayed away from the polls, but independent electoral observers said the figure was closer to 60 percent.
The PRI, which has ruled Mexico for 67 years, has historically held overwhelming political power in the state, controlling 68 of the 76 town halls.
